UNDERSTANDING YOUR OPTIONS

When a commercial dispute enters arbitration, knowing what happens next matters.

The arbitration agreement

Whether SIAC has jurisdiction, how many arbitrators will sit and which rules apply all start with the wording of your arbitration clause. It is usually the first document we review.

Once proceedings begin

Deadlines under the SIAC Rules can be short. A Response to the Notice of Arbitration is generally due within 14 days. Responding to a Notice of Arbitration, choosing an arbitrator and raising any jurisdictional objection each need early, careful attention.

The strategic picture

Cost, timing, confidentiality and where an award may need to be enforced all influence strategy. Considering them early helps businesses decide how to proceed with a clear view of the process.

01 — YOUR ARBITRATION CLAUSE

Understanding the arbitration clause in your contract.

+

SIAC becomes relevant where the contract contains an arbitration clause naming SIAC. This is common in shareholder agreements, joint ventures, supply and distribution contracts, and investment arrangements with Singapore-related counterparties.

Points that can matter include the exact wording of the clause, which entities are bound, whether Singapore is the seat or merely the venue, and the number of arbitrators. These details shape what happens if a dispute arises.

Indian contracts often name Singapore as the “venue” rather than the “seat”. The seat decides which country’s courts supervise the arbitration and which law governs any challenge to the award, so this distinction can change your strategy.

Where a clause is unclear or names an institution inconsistently, careful analysis is needed before deciding on next steps.

02 — YOUR FIRST DEADLINE

Responding to a Notice of Arbitration within the deadline.

+

A Notice of Arbitration formally commences the arbitration. Under the SIAC Rules, the respondent is generally expected to file a response within 14 days of receiving the Notice (or of commencement, if later; SIAC Rules 2025, Rule 7.1), so the notice should be reviewed as soon as it arrives.

Early questions usually include: does a valid arbitration agreement exist and does it cover this dispute; is the claim brought against the right party; how should the arbitrator be nominated; and is there a counterclaim to consider.

It is also sensible to preserve relevant documents and correspondence from the outset.

03 — THE TRIBUNAL

How an arbitral tribunal is formed and decides a dispute.

+

Instead of a court, an arbitral tribunal hears both sides and issues a binding award. The Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) is the independent institution that administers the arbitration.

For arbitrations seated in Singapore, the International Arbitration Act 1994 and the Singapore courts support and supervise the process, which is generally private and confidential.

The SIAC Rules 2025 offer a streamlined procedure for claims up to S$1 million, an expedited procedure for claims up to S$10 million, and emergency arbitrator relief before the tribunal is formed.

04 — COST, TIME AND ENFORCEMENT

Understanding the costs, timing and enforcement of an award.

+

Costs typically include SIAC administrative fees, the tribunal’s fees and legal costs. How long a matter takes depends on its complexity, the number of parties and whether the streamlined or expedited procedure applies. Third-party funding is permitted for international arbitration in Singapore.

Where an award is not complied with voluntarily, it may need to be enforced. Awards made in Singapore-seated arbitrations can be enforced in more than 170 countries under the New York Convention. India enforces awards from Singapore-seated arbitrations as foreign awards, and the grounds to resist them are limited.

We aim to give clients a realistic view of cost, timing and enforcement at the outset, so decisions can be made with that in mind.

Frequently asked questions

What is arbitration in Singapore?

Arbitration is a private dispute resolution process where parties agree to have disputes decided by an independent tribunal rather than courts. Where Singapore is the seat, the arbitration is governed by the International Arbitration Act 1994 and supervised by the Singapore courts. Indian businesses often choose Singapore as a neutral seat with experienced arbitrators, supportive courts and awards that Indian courts recognise as foreign awards.

When should a business consider arbitration?

Businesses should consider arbitration when disputes involve cross-border elements, foreign counterparties or shareholders, or offshore holding structures, or where neutrality, confidentiality, and enforceability of outcomes are critical.

What is SIAC?

The Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) is a leading global arbitration institution administering domestic and international arbitrations around the world. SIAC also has representative offices in India, in Delhi, Mumbai and GIFT City.

Why do Indian businesses choose SIAC?

SIAC offers a neutral and well-regarded arbitral framework, experienced international tribunals, procedural efficiency, and, where the arbitration is seated in Singapore, awards enforceable in more than 170 countries under the New York Convention. This makes SIAC a common choice for Indian businesses in cross-border joint venture, shareholder and commercial disputes. Indian parties have been among SIAC's top three foreign users over the past decade.

What is the SICC?

The SICC is part of the High Court of Singapore for international commercial disputes, with a bench of Singapore and international judges. Disputes usually reach the SICC through a jurisdiction clause in the contract.

When should we use the SICC?

The SICC suits parties who want a court judgment with a right of appeal, the ability to join third parties more easily, or a public precedent. Arbitration may suit parties who want confidentiality, a choice of arbitrators and the widest international enforcement. The choice is usually made when the contract is drafted, through the dispute resolution clause.

Can an SICC judgment be enforced in India?

Singapore is a reciprocating territory under section 44A of the Code of Civil Procedure, and Indian courts have treated the SICC as a superior court for this purpose. A judgment can therefore be executed in India as if it were an Indian decree, but it can be refused on the grounds in section 13, including where a party did not submit to the SICC's jurisdiction. A clear, written SICC jurisdiction clause signed by the right parties is essential.

Do we need an arbitration clause to commence SIAC arbitration?

Generally, yes. Arbitration requires a valid arbitration agreement, usually contained in the main commercial contract, such as a joint venture, shareholders', supply or distribution agreement. Parties can also agree to arbitrate after a dispute has arisen. If your clause names Singapore only as the venue, it is worth checking whether Singapore is also the seat, because the seat decides which courts supervise the arbitration. We also advise on strategic options where arbitration clauses are absent or defective.

Can a Singapore arbitration award be enforced in India?

Yes. Singapore-seated arbitral awards are enforceable in more than 170 countries under the New York Convention, making SIAC arbitration particularly effective for cross-border shareholder and commercial disputes. In India, awards from Singapore-seated arbitrations are enforced under Part II of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996. The application is made to the relevant High Court, which does not review the merits of the dispute and can refuse enforcement only on the limited grounds in section 48.

What are the costs of arbitration?

Costs include arbitrator fees, institutional fees, and legal costs, and vary based on dispute value and complexity. SIAC publishes a schedule of fees and a cost calculator. The tribunal can order the unsuccessful party to bear some or all of the costs, and third-party funding is permitted for international arbitration in Singapore.

Can we get urgent relief over assets in India?

Yes. Under the SIAC Rules, an emergency arbitrator can be appointed before the tribunal is formed, and an application can now be made even before the Notice of Arbitration is filed. Where the arbitration is seated in Singapore, Indian courts can also grant interim relief under section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996.

Can two Indian companies choose SIAC or a Singapore seat?

Yes. Two Indian parties can choose a foreign seat such as Singapore, and the resulting award can be enforced in India as a foreign award. The clause still needs careful drafting, and Indian law may continue to govern the substance of the contract.

Can our Indian lawyers be part of the team?

Yes. In international arbitrations seated in Singapore, parties can be represented by lawyers of their choice, including foreign lawyers. We can work alongside your Indian counsel, who advise on Indian law, while we handle the Singapore and SIAC aspects of the matter.

Can hearings take place in India or online?

Yes. The seat is a legal concept, not a physical location. Hearings in a Singapore-seated arbitration can be held in India, elsewhere or online where the tribunal considers it appropriate after consulting the parties, without changing the seat.

What if the other side has already sued us in India?

If the dispute is covered by a valid arbitration agreement, you can ask the Indian court to refer the parties to arbitration under section 45 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996. It is best to act early, before taking steps that could be seen as accepting the court's jurisdiction.
